newsitem.title: UK: British truckers face delays after French blockade.
newsitem.headline: British truckers face delays after French blockade.

text.p: More than 750 trucks were backed up on a motorway near the British port of Dover on Wednesday because of a French fishermen's blockade of the ports of Dunkirk, Calais and Boulogne.

Thousands of holidaymakers also faced delays because ferries were diverted to the Belgian port of Zeebrugge following the French fishermen's protest over European Union regulations on net sizes, which began on Tuesday.

A spokesman for the port of Dover said 750 trucks were parked on the M20 motorway near Dover. It was hoped to clear the backlog during the course of the day but queues could build up again over night.
The Managing Director of P and O European Ferries, Russ Peters, said he was considering taking legal action against the French fishermamn.
"We can take out an injunction against these fishermen," he told BBC television. "I regret there will be many hours of delay for the truckers today."
Drivers in the makeshift lorry park on the M20 said the delays were worse than they had feared.
"We heard it was bad, but not as bad as this," said one driver. "We thought we would have to wait a couple of hours, not all night."
Normally, 2,000 trucks a day take the ferries between Dover and Calais, a journey of about 90 minutes, while the trip to Zeebrugge takes more than four hours.
